newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Headlines - June 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Headlines - June 19.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- WEN WEI PO -- Chinese Vice-Premier Qian Qichen said maintaining Hong Kong's long-term prosperity was an important strategic task, and its core lay in carrying out the "one country, two systems" principle.

-- TA KUNG PAO -- A new world record will be created during Hong Kong's handover -- the biggest karaoke chorus -- during the yacht parade in the Victoria Harbour on the handover night, as most of Hong Kong's six million people can sing songs together.

-- EXPRESS NEWS -- Although British Prime Minister Tony Blair will not attend the swearing-in of the provisional legislature, the British Foreign Office invited all members of the provisional body to a farewell party on June 30.

-- Half of Hong Kong people surveyed say they are "Hong Kongers", while only 25 percent describe themselves as Chinese. The survey shows those who prefer to be "Hong Kongers" hold a suspicious and unwilling attitude towards the handover.

-- MING PAO -- The Chinese leadership urged all departments involved in relations with Taiwan to "do more and talk less". They also hoped some breakthrough would take place regarding direct shipping and trade relations between the two sides.

-- ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- The head of a Hong Kong property and construction association said it will not take any measures to intervene in the property market, and added the association was strongly against imposing extra taxes to bring down prices.

-- ECONOMIC TIMES -- C.Y. Leung, Chief Executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa's advisor on property policy, said new measures on housing would curb speculation but would not damage the economy. Leung said he would submit his report to Tung within the week.

-- SING TAO -- The amount of counterfeit money in Guangzhou has increased in recent years. More than 170,000 notes worth over HK$5 million were discovered in the first five months of this year, representing a 90 percent increase from last year.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Governor Chris Patten cast doubts on the ability of Hong Kong's future leaders to reverse the territory's social, economic and political values. He emphasised the need for continuity, but admitted that he and post-handover leader Tung held different philosophies.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- China Resources Enterprise was acquiring a substantial stake in a medium-sized Hong Kong bank in an apparent bid to gain a bigger presence in the territory's financial services industry.
